# Step-by-Step Guide: Digital Collaging & Style Transfer

## Digital Collaging in Photoshop

### 1. Preparation
- Create a new document (3000×2000px at 300dpi for print quality)
- Organize your source materials in a dedicated folder
- Sketch a rough composition plan to guide your process

### 2. Building Your Base
- Start with a background layer or texture that sets the mood
- Use File > Place Embedded to import your first element
- Scale and position using Transform tools (Ctrl/Cmd+T)
- Repeat for major compositional elements

### 3. Blending Techniques
- For each element, add a layer mask (click the mask icon in Layers panel)
- Use soft brushes (20-40% opacity) on masks to create soft transitions
- Try blending modes: Overlay for textures, Multiply for shadows, Screen for light
- Adjust opacity of layers to control their prominence

### 4. Cohesive Integration
- Add an adjustment layer (Curves or Color Balance) at the top of your stack
- Click "Create clipping mask" to apply it to specific layers
- Use Hue/Saturation to match color tones across elements
- Apply Filter > Blur > Gaussian Blur subtly to elements that appear too sharp

### 5. Adding Dimension
- Create shadow layers beneath elements (black brush at low opacity)
- Add highlights with a soft white brush on new layers set to Overlay
- Consider atmospheric perspective—distant elements should be lighter/less saturated

## Style Transfer in Procreate

### 1. Setting Up
- Import your base composition or photograph
- Create a new layer for each style element
- Set up a custom palette based on your inspiration source

### 2. Applying Artistic Style
- Use textured brushes that match your target style (impressionist, graphic, etc.)
- Work in broad strokes first to establish overall feel
- Reduce brush size for details in focal areas
- Vary pressure sensitivity for dynamic line weight

### 3. Texture Integration
- Import texture files as new layers
- Set blending mode to Overlay or Soft Light
- Adjust opacity to 15-30% for subtle effect
- Use the Liquify tool to conform textures to your forms

### 4. Refinement
- Use the Smudge tool with a textured brush to blend transitions
- Add noise (Add > Noise) at 3-5% for unified grain
- Use Gaussian blur on background elements to create depth
- Enhance contrast in focal areas with Curves adjustment

### 5. Final Touches
- Add a subtle vignette to draw attention inward
- Apply a unified color grade across all layers
- Consider a very subtle paper texture overlay at 10-15% opacity
- Export at appropriate resolution for your intended use

## Pro Tips
- Work non-destructively with adjustment layers and smart objects
- Save versions at key stages so you can backtrack if needed
- Step away periodically to view with fresh eyes
- Consider printing drafts to see how the composition works physically

# 5 Super Simple Photoshop Blending Techniques

I understand you need straightforward solutions. Here are the absolute simplest ways to blend images in Photoshop for quick results:

## 1. Quick Layer Masks
- Paste your image on top of background
- Click the "Add Layer Mask" button (rectangle with circle) at bottom of Layers panel
- Use a soft black brush to erase/blend edges where needed
- That's it! No complex selections needed

## 2. Blend Modes in One Click
- Place your image on top of background
- In Layers panel, change blend mode from "Normal" to:
  * "Multiply" for darker elements to blend
  * "Screen" for lighter elements to blend
  * "Overlay" for high-contrast blending
- Adjust opacity slider if effect is too strong

## 3. Auto-Select and Remove Background
- Select image layer
- Click "Select Subject" button in top options bar
- Press Delete to remove background
- Place over your new background
- Done!

## 4. One-Step Color Matching
- Select the layer you want to match
- Go to Image > Adjustments > Match Color
- Under Source, select your open document
- Under Layer, choose the image whose color you want to match
- Click OK

## 5. Quick Gradient Blend
- Place images side by side on separate layers
- Add layer mask to top image
- Select Gradient Tool (G)
- Draw a simple left-to-right gradient on the mask
- Images blend seamlessly where they meet

## Bonus: Instant Polished Look
- Select all layers and press Ctrl+Alt+Shift+E to create merged copy on top
- Go to Filter > Camera Raw Filter
- Click "Auto" for instant color correction
- Slightly increase Clarity and Vibrance sliders
- Click OK

These techniques require minimal technical skill but deliver professional-looking results quickly. Just focus on these basics and you'll have your project finished in no time!
